deep.reconstruction:
This page is a draft of Riemann's 'Theorie der Abel'schen Functionen' (Crelle 54, 1857). It covers the end of the treatment of everywhere-finite integrals (first kind) and the beginning of integrals of the second kind.

(A) End of the first-kind argument, continued from the previous page. Let w_1,...,w_p be everywhere-finite functions on the cut surface T' with no linear relation with constant coefficients. Let k_i^(nu), nu = 1..2p, be their periodicity moduli across the cross-cuts. Put w = sum_i alpha_i w_i + const with alpha_i = gamma_i + i delta_i. Then the modulus of w on the nu-th cut is k^(nu) = sum_i alpha_i k_i^(nu). Its real part is sum_i (gamma_i Re k_i^(nu) - delta_i Im k_i^(nu)) [explicit formula mine].

This gives 2p real linear equations in the 2p real unknowns gamma_i, delta_i. The determinant does not vanish. Otherwise some nonzero choice would give a w with purely imaginary moduli. Its real part would then be a single-valued harmonic function, finite everywhere on the closed surface, hence constant by the Dirichlet-principle uniqueness. That would contradict the linear independence of the w_i [the uniqueness step is stated on the previous page; its explicit use here is my filling].

Hence the alpha_i can be chosen so that the real parts of the moduli of w take arbitrary prescribed values. Since an everywhere-finite function is determined up to a constant by those real parts, every everywhere-finite function equals alpha_1 w_1 + ... + alpha_p w_p + const.

The partly struck-out text continues: as long as mu < p, a combination c_1 w_1 + ... + c_mu w_mu + const has only 2mu real parameters. It cannot meet 2p arbitrary conditions, so further independent functions exist. Conversely, a (p+1)-th function w_{p+1} would have to be expressible in this form. Result: exactly p linearly independent integrals of the first kind.

(B) Heading 'II. Functions which become infinite of the first order at one point of the surface (Integrale zweiter Gattung).'

First draft claim: a function w that near a point behaves like b/(z - s), and is otherwise continuous, is completely determined by b and the real parts of its periodicity moduli. A variant is noted for the point where z = infinity.

(C) 'Zur Vereinfachung des Folgenden': definition of a function infinitely small of the first order at a point of T, i.e. a local uniformizing parameter. The wording is roughly: its logarithm increases by 2 pi i under one positive circuit around the point, within a surrounding piece of surface. Examples:
- at an ordinary point z = s, the parameter is z - s;
- at a winding (branch) point where the surface winds mu times, it is (z - s)^(1/mu);
- at z = infinity, presumably 1/z (or z^(-1/mu)) [mine].
Such a function must stay finite and nonzero elsewhere in the neighbourhood.

With t such a local parameter, the singular part of a function is described as an expression like a log t + b/t + c/t^2 + ..., whose subtraction makes the function continuous at the point. This relies on the 'known theorems on expansion of a function in power series'.

(D) Final redraft: a function w that becomes infinite at a point (where z = a) like b/t (b/(z - s) at an ordinary point), and otherwise stays continuous, is determined up to an additive constant by b and the real parts of its periodicity moduli. It exists by the Dirichlet principle. Hence, for t an arbitrary function infinitely small of the first order at that point and otherwise finite, one gets the integral of the second kind with prescribed pole b/t. The text breaks off here; the next page jumps to section 10 (rational transformations).
errors: No mathematical errors visible. The first draft says 'völlig bestimmt' (completely determined) for the second-kind function; the redraft correctly adds 'bis auf eine additive Constante' (up to an additive constant).
Nonvanishing of the 2p x 2p real determinant is not stated on this page. It follows from the uniqueness argument (purely imaginary moduli imply constant) given on the previous page.

At a branch point the expression b/(z-s) equals b/t^mu, which is not a simple pole in the local parameter. The redraft's use of b/t in the local parameter t fixes this; the earlier formulation with b/(z-s) only fits ordinary points.

results.what: Every everywhere-finite integral on a genus-p surface is a linear combination of p independent ones plus a constant. The coefficients can be chosen to give arbitrary real parts of the 2p periods.
results.modern_name: dim H^0(K) = p; real parts of periods of holomorphic differentials can be prescribed (Riemann bilinear / period lattice nondegeneracy)

results.what: Definition of a function 'unendlich klein von der ersten Ordnung' at a point: z-s at ordinary points, (z-s)^(1/mu) at a winding point of mu sheets.
results.modern_name: local uniformizing parameter / local coordinate on a Riemann surface

results.what: Existence and uniqueness (up to a constant) of an integral of the second kind with prescribed pole b/t, given by b and the real parts of its periods, via the Dirichlet principle.
results.modern_name: abelian integrals (differentials) of the second kind; normalized meromorphic differentials

deep.surprise_reason: This is a working draft of §§3-4 of Riemann's published 1857 Abelian functions paper (integrals of the first and second kind, local parameter). The content is well known as his; only draft wording differs.

checkable.asserts: The real part of a period alpha*k is linear in gamma and delta: Re k = gamma*Re k_i - delta*Im k_i. This gives 2p real equations in 2p real unknowns.
At a winding point with z-s = t^mu, the expression b/(z-s) has a pole of order mu in the local parameter t. This is why the redraft uses b/t.
The parameter (z-s)^(1/mu) uniformizes a mu-sheeted winding point.

transcription_corrections: Top lines: read roughly 'können so bestimmt werden, daß die reellen Theile der Periodicitätsmoduln von w beliebig gegebene Werthe erhalten, und folglich ... läßt sich daher jede überall endlich bleibende Function in der Form alpha_1 w_1 + ... + alpha_p w_p + const darstellen'.
'c_1 w_1 + c_2 w_2 + c_3 w_3 ...' is likely 'c_1 w_1 + c_2 w_2 + ... + c_mu w_mu + const', since the context is mu < p.

In the definition of 'unendlich klein von der ersten Ordnung', 'log(z-s)' is probably a conflation. The image suggests: 'wenn ihr log bei einem einmaligen positiven Umlauf um diesen Punkt ... um 2πi wächst ... Für einen Punkt z = s ist z - s unendlich klein von der ersten Ordnung, wenn dort kein Windungspunkt stattfindet, und (z-s)^{1/μ}, wenn die Fläche sich μ mal herumwindet.'
'für einen Punkt der Fläche [?] wird wie b/(z-s)' is likely 'für einen Punkt der Fläche unstetig wird wie b/(z-s)'.
After 'a log t + b/t + c/tt' the phrase reads roughly 'in eine stetige Function verwandelt wird' (subtraction of the singular part).

Bottom: 'Bezeichnet daher t eine beliebige Function, die in diesem Punkte der Fläche T unendlich klein der ersten Ordnung wird und übrigens endlich bleibt' ('Function w' there is likely just 'Function').
